state_program_name: Nonmedical home health services provider (ODH nonmedical license, ORC Chapter 3740 / OAC Chapter 3701-60); Medicaid pathways: ODA PASSPORT personal care (OAC 173-39) and ODM Ohio Home Care Waiver / Medicaid personal care aide (OAC 5160-46)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** delivers nonmedical home health services in Ohio in compliance with state law. The services are home health aide services and personal care services, including help with self-administration of medication (ORC 3740.01; OAC 3701-60-01). It is written for the following pathways:

- **ODH nonmedical home health services license** under ORC Chapter 3740 and OAC Chapter 3701-60.
- **ODA PASSPORT personal care** certification under OAC Chapter 173-39 (and Older Americans Act personal care under OAC 173-3-06.5).
- **ODM Ohio Home Care Waiver / Medicaid personal care aide** services under OAC Chapter 5160-46 and related ODM rules.

The manual has four goals:

1. Give the Ohio Department of Health (ODH) the written services-and-policies, criminal records check, hours of operation and service-area materials it reviews with a license application or renewal.
2. Give ODA and ODM reviewers the written policies, staffing, training, supervision, documentation, incident-reporting and records standards that certified and enrolled providers must follow.
3. Give owners, administrators, supervisors and aides one consistent source of procedures for day-to-day work.
4. Protect clients' health, safety, dignity, privacy and rights, and protect the agency from unlicensed practice, billing errors and enforcement action.

This manual covers **nonmedical** services only. Nursing tasks and other skilled care are outside its scope. If the agency enrolls for a service with a nursing-task component, such as the home care attendant service in OAC 5160-46-06.1, add policies that cover it before delivering that service.

This manual is a compliance tool and not legal advice. If a policy conflicts with a current statute or rule, the statute or rule controls.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**1. Customize it first.** This manual is a template. Before use, replace every placeholder (**[AGENCY NAME]**, owner and administrator names, addresses, phone and email, days and hours of operation, service area, back-up staffing contacts and similar fields) with the agency's actual information. Delete or modify any pathway that the agency will not use (for example, skip the ODA PASSPORT sections if the agency will not seek ODA certification). Do not leave bracketed text in any copy given to a regulator, employee or client.

**2. Adopt it formally.** The agency's governing body (owner, board of directors, members or managers, as applicable) must review and adopt the customized manual and record the adoption in its minutes or by signed resolution. Record the effective date and version number on the cover page.

**3. Train staff.** Every owner, administrator, supervisor and aide must be trained on the manual. The agency must:
- Train staff on the manual at hire and before any in-person client contact, and again whenever it changes.
- Keep signed acknowledgments and training records in each personnel file.
- Use the orientation, in-service, supervision and conduct sections as the basis for the training the ODA and ODM rules require (see OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(3) and OAC 5160-46-04).

**4. Keep it current.** Laws and rules change. Assign a named person to do the following:
- Review the manual at least annually and whenever a cited rule, fee, form or EVV requirement changes.
- Subscribe to ODA rule-update emails, as OAC 173-39-02(B)(13) requires of certified providers, and monitor ODH and ODM announcements.
- Check the current text of rules marked as time-sensitive. For example, read the current OAC 5160-46-06 before billing.
- Date each revision, have the governing body adopt it, retrain staff, and keep superseded versions on file.
- Give ODH written notice within 10 days of any change to the application information on file (OAC 3701-60-03(G)-(J)).

**5. Navigate with the citations and Appendix A.** Each policy cites the rule it implements. **Appendix A** maps every item in the official documents the state uses to review this manual to the policy that satisfies it. A reviewer can start from an official item and go straight to the answering policy. Staff can start from a policy and see why it exists.

**6. Keep it accessible.** Keep a current copy at the business site, where records must be available to regulators. Give each employee access to the sections that apply to their role. Keep the manual consistent with client service plans, which control the specific tasks and hours authorized for each client.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

### Governing statutes and rules

The manual is built on the following authorities, cited by their exact cite text.

**Licensure (ODH): ORC Chapter 3740 and OAC Chapter 3701-60**
- **ORC 3740.01**: definitions, including nonmedical home health services, direct care, nonagency provider and immediate family member.
- **ORC 3740.02(A)(2), (B)(2)**: no agency or nonagency provider may provide, or hold itself out as providing, nonmedical home health services without a current nonmedical or skilled license.
- **ORC 3740.03(B)**: application contents (owner fingerprints, Secretary of State filings, notarized identity affidavit, criminal records check policy, days and hours, services and policies, service area, $20,000 bond if new, $250 fee). A waiver applies if the provider is ODA-certified (ORC 3740.03(B)(3)).
- **ORC 3740.04**: issuance of licenses.
- **ORC 3740.05**: three-year validity and renewal.
- **ORC 3740.07**: enforcement (refusal, limitation, suspension, revocation, probation or reprimand under ORC Chapter 119).
- **ORC 3740.10**: rulemaking.
- **ORC 3740.11**: criminal records check of direct-care applicants and employees.
- **OAC 3701-60-01**: definitions, including direct care, disqualifying information, and the self-administration-of-medication limits in paragraph (Y).
- **OAC 3701-60-02**: applicability. Since Oct. 1, 2022, no provider may deliver or advertise nonmedical home health services without a license, and violation is a criminal misdemeanor.
- **OAC 3701-60-03(B)**: nonmedical license application contents.
- **OAC 3701-60-03(G)-(J)**: ODH information requests (14 days), timely renewal (90 days before expiration), change notice (10 days) and license term.
- **OAC 3701-60-04**: enforcement and hearing and dispute-resolution rights.
- **OAC 3701-60-05**: state and national database review.
- **OAC 3701-60-06**: criminal records check requirements.
- **OAC 3701-60-07**: conditional employment.

**ODA PASSPORT and Older Americans Act personal care**
- **OAC 173-39-02(A)**: requirements to become certified (business site and locked records, $1M commercial liability insurance, incident policy, EVV).
- **OAC 173-39-02(B)(3)**: reporting duties (suspected abuse, neglect and exploitation; significant changes; contact changes; 30 days' notice before ending service).
- **OAC 173-39-02(B)(4), (B)(8)**: confidentiality and ethical/professional standards.
- **OAC 173-39-02(B)(10)-(13)**: records retention, access, payment in full, rule updates.
- **OAC 173-39-02(C)(1)**: agency disclosures, attestations and written policies.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(A)-(B)**: personal care definition and provider types.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(2)**: availability and staffing.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(3)(a)**: initial PCA qualifications.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(3)(b)-(f)**: orientation, in-service and verification.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(4)**: PCA supervisors and visits.
- **OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5)-(6)**: policies and service verification.
- **OAC 173-3-06.5**: Older Americans Act personal care.
- **OAC 5160-31-03**: PASSPORT eligibility and enrollment.

**ODM Ohio Home Care Waiver and Medicaid personal care aide**
- **OAC 5160-46-04(A)-(D)**: scope of aide services and medication limits.
- **OAC 5160-46-04(E)-(H)**: provider and aide requirements.
- **OAC 5160-46-04(I)-(J)**: clinical record.
- **OAC 5160-44-31(A)-(B)**: waiver provider conditions of participation.
- **OAC 5160-44-31(B)(14)-(15)**: visit documentation and retention.
- **OAC 5160-44-31(B)(17), (B)(20)**: 24-hour notices and termination of service.
- **OAC 5160-44-31(C)-(F)**: EVV, prohibited conduct, legal decision-makers.
- **OAC 5160-44-05**: HCBS waiver incident management.
- **OAC 5160-44-02**: person-centered planning.
- **OAC 5160-46-06**: Ohio Home Care Waiver billing and covered services. Read the current text before billing.
- **OAC 5160-46-06.1**: home care attendant. This applies only if the agency enrolls for that service, and it includes a nursing-task component outside nonmedical scope.
- **OAC 5160-58-04**: Medicaid personal care aide service (T1019), subject to Electronic Visit Verification.

**Wage and hour**
- **Ohio Const. Art. II §34a; ORC Chapter 4111; Ohio Dept. of Commerce 2026 minimum wage notice**: the 2026 Ohio minimum wage is $11.00/hour for non-tipped employees. It applies to employers above $405,000 in gross receipts; smaller employers stay at the federal floor. Employers must display the official 2026 poster.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Ohio Department of Health (ODH), Home Health Agency Licensure** | Issues, renews and enforces the nonmedical home health services license; may refuse, limit, suspend, revoke or place a license on probation | https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/home-health-agencies/home-health-agency-licensure/home-health-agency-licensure (no phone or email is listed in the source material; use the website) |
| **ODH Revenue Processing #3506** | Receives mailed license applications and fee payments | P.O. Box 15278, Columbus, OH 43215 |
| **Ohio Department of Aging (ODA)** | Certifies PASSPORT personal care providers; oversees Older Americans Act personal care | 1-800-266-4346 (main line); https://aging.ohio.gov/care-and-living/get-help/home-and-community-care/passport-participant-direction |
| **Council on Aging / Area Agencies on Aging** | Recommend prospective PASSPORT providers to ODA before certification and administer PASSPORT locally | https://www.help4seniors.org/service-providers/passport-assisted-living/prospective-provider-information/ (find the agency for the service area) |
| **Ohio Department of Medicaid (ODM)** | Medicaid provider enrollment, Ohio Home Care Waiver, fee schedules, EVV and program integrity | 1-800-686-1516 (ODM Integrated Help Desk); https://medicaid.ohio.gov/resources-for-providers/billing/fee-schedule-and-rates/schedules-and-rates |
| **Ohio Department of Commerce, Wage and Hour** | Administers the Ohio minimum wage and poster requirement | https://com.ohio.gov/about-us/media-center/news/ohio%20minimum%20wage%20set%20to%20increase%20in%202026 |

Verify all contact details with the regulator before relying on them. Enter the agency's own regulator contacts and account numbers in the customized manual.

### Official documents the state uses to review this manual

ODH publishes **no separate policy checklist** for the nonmedical license. The controlling list of what a complete application must contain is the rule itself. The ODH "Nonmedical Home Health Services License Application" accompanies that rule. ODA likewise does not publish a policy-manual checklist. Reviewers therefore use the following official documents, and the manual is organized to follow their paragraph numbers:

1. **OAC 3701-60-03, paragraph (B)** (ODH; effective Jan. 27, 2023): the nonmedical home health services license application contents. The policy and plan items are (B)(3)(d), (g), (h) and (i): the list of nonmedical services and related policies and procedures, the written criminal records check policy, the days and hours of operation, and the geographic area served. Under paragraph (E), items (B)(3)(d) to (k) are waived for providers showing ODA certification under ORC 173.391. Under paragraph (F), items (B)(3)(d) to (i) are waived for providers accredited by an approved national organization.
2. **OAC 3701-60-06** (ODH; effective Jan. 27, 2023): sets the content of the written criminal records check policy required by 3701-60-03(B)(3)(g). Its items are the rule's own duties on the chief administrator.
3. **OAC 173-39-02** (ODA; effective Apr. 1, 2025): required written policies and reporting duties for ODA-certified agency providers.
4. **OAC 173-39-02.11** (ODA; effective July 1, 2024): PASSPORT personal care. Paragraph (C)(5), "Provider policies," is the nearest thing to an enumerated policy list. The staffing, orientation, training, supervision and service-verification duties are also addressed.

**Appendix A maps every official item from these documents to the policy in this manual that satisfies it.** Where an item is a duty and not a literally required "policy," the manual still addresses it, so every item has a mapped answer. Disclosure paperwork (ownership disclosures, organization table, attestations) is not policy content and is completed on the agency's application forms. The ODM rules (OAC 5160-46-04, 5160-44-31, 5160-44-05 and 5160-58-04) are addressed in the manual's operating policies but are not tied to a published checklist.

### Customization, adoption, currency and training

- **Customize**: complete every **[AGENCY NAME]** and other placeholder before use.
- **Adopt**: the governing body must formally adopt the manual and each revision.
- **Keep current**: review at least annually and whenever a rule, fee or form changes, and report application changes to ODH within 10 days.
- **Train**: all staff must be trained on the manual at hire and on each revision, with signed acknowledgments retained.

Operating without a current license, or advertising services without one, is a criminal offense under OAC 3701-60-02, and ODH may take enforcement action under ORC 3740.07 and OAC 3701-60-04. Compliance with this manual is therefore a condition of employment and of continued operation.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines nonmedical home health services (home health aide services, personal care services incl. self-administration help), direct care, nonagency provider (not more than 2 unrelated individuals excluded) and immediate family member.

citations.title: License requirements
citations.requirement: An agency or nonagency provider may not provide, or hold itself out as providing, nonmedical home health services without a current nonmedical or skilled license.

citations.title: Applications for licensure (nonmedical)
citations.requirement: Application: owner fingerprints, SOS filings, notarized identity affidavit, criminal records check policy, days/hours, services and policies, service area, $20,000 bond if new, $250 fee. Waiver if ODA-certified (B)(3).

citations.title: Issuance of licenses
citations.requirement: ODH reviews each application. It issues the license once the fee is paid and the ORC 3740.03 requirements are shown, unless 3740.07 applies. A site visit is mandated only for the Medicare-certification basis.

citations.title: Validity, renewal of licenses
citations.requirement: License is valid three years. Renewal requires the $250 renewal fee and a showing of continued compliance with ORC 3740.03. ODH may adjust the initial renewal date.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: ODH may refuse to issue or renew, limit, suspend or revoke a license, or impose probation or reprimand. Actions follow ORC Chapter 119.

citations.title: Rules
citations.requirement: Director of Health adopts rules on application and renewal forms and procedures, grounds for enforcement, and dispute resolution/appeals, in consultation with ODA and the Medicaid Director.

citations.title: Criminal records check
citations.requirement: Agency may not employ direct-care applicants or employees who appear in the listed databases or have disqualifying offenses. Requires database review and BCI check. Conditional hire allowed if the check is requested within 5 business days. Reports are confidential.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines direct care, disqualifying information, nonmedical home health services and personal care services. Para (Y) lists what staff may do for self-administration of medication (remind, hand, open container, assist).

citations.title: Applicability
citations.requirement: Since Oct 1, 2022, no provider may deliver or advertise nonmedical home health services without a license. Violation is a 2nd-degree misdemeanor on a first offense and a 1st-degree misdemeanor for each later offense.

citations.title: Nonmedical license application contents
citations.requirement: Complete application: prescribed forms, $250 non-refundable fee (cashier's check or money order), owners/officers, services list and related policies, SOS documents, written criminal records check policy, hours, area, fingerprints, $20,000 bond.

citations.title: ODH information requests, renewal timing, change notice, term
citations.requirement: Reply to ODH information requests within 14 days of mailing. Renewal is timely if filed at least 90 days before expiration. Give ODH written notice within 10 days of any application change. License lasts 3 years.

citations.title: Enforcement
citations.requirement: Director may deny, suspend or revoke for material misrepresentation, failure to timely renew, or no longer meeting requirements. Hearing right under ORC 119. Informal dispute resolution is available after a denial.

citations.title: State and national database review
citations.requirement: Before the criminal records check, check SAM, OIG LEIE, DODD abuse registry, sex offender database, ODRC inmate database and Ohio nurse aide registry for each direct-care applicant and employee. Disqualifying information bars employment.

citations.title: Requirements for criminal records check
citations.requirement: BCI check of each direct-care applicant; employees rechecked within 30 days after each 5-year hire anniversary. FBI check if not an Ohio resident for 5 years. Applicant notice, fee rules and fingerprint forms are specified.

citations.title: Conditional employment
citations.requirement: Conditional hire only if the database review is clear, fingerprints are submitted before start, and the check is requested within 5 business days. Terminate if results are not received within 60 days or show a disqualifying offense.

citations.title: ODA certification: requirements to become certified
citations.requirement: Business site with locked record storage accessible to ODA/ODM/HHS/Auditor. $1M commercial liability insurance covering theft/property damage, plus written instructions for loss claims. Written incident policy. EVV. Email/phone on file.

citations.title: ODA certified provider reporting duties
citations.requirement: Report suspected abuse/neglect/exploitation to APS and notify ODA or its designee within 1 business day. Report significant changes within 1 business day. Report contact changes within 7 days. Give 30 days' written notice before ending service, with exceptions.

citations.title: ODA confidentiality and ethical/professional standards
citations.requirement: Comply with confidentiality laws (HIPAA 45 CFR 160/162/164, 42 CFR 431.300-307). Prohibits gifts or tips, sexual conduct, alcohol or drugs, distractions, sleeping, visitors, selling to clients, social media photos without consent.

citations.title: ODA records retention, access, payment, rule updates
citations.requirement: Keep service records 6 years after payment (or until review/audit ends) and qualification records for employment plus 6 years. Give ODA/ODM/HHS/Auditor immediate access. Accept the agreed rate as payment in full. Subscribe to ODA rule emails.

citations.title: ODA agency provider disclosures, attestations, policies
citations.requirement: Agencies disclose owners (and any felony convictions) and an organization table, and show an active SOS registration. They attest to 45 CFR 80.4, EEO, wage-hour and workers' comp compliance, and tax payment. Written policies must require staff to meet (B)(8) conduct standards.

citations.title: ODA personal care: definition and provider types
citations.requirement: Personal care is hands-on ADL/IADL help, home management, help with self-administration of medications, homemaker tasks and errands, as authorized in the service plan. Respite is excluded. Providers are ODA-certified agencies or participant-directed providers.

citations.title: ODA personal care: availability and staffing
citations.requirement: Accept a referral only with adequate PCA and PCA-supervisor staffing for the authorized hours. An RN or LPN supervises PCAs during all scheduled hours. Maintain a back-up plan for when no PCA or supervisor is available.

citations.title: ODA personal care: initial PCA qualifications
citations.requirement: PCA must be an STNA, meet Medicare HHA standards, have 1 year of supervised aide experience plus competency evaluation, complete COALA or a vocational program, or complete a 30-hour program covering the listed topics.

citations.title: ODA personal care: orientation, in-service, verification
citations.requirement: Orientation before any in-person client contact (7 listed topics). Six hours of ODA-approved in-service every 12 months (orientation excluded). Keep training certificates, nurse aide registry printout, and prior-employment proof.

citations.title: ODA personal care: PCA supervisors and visits
citations.requirement: Only an RN or LPN under RN direction may supervise. In-person home visit and activity plan before or at the first episode. Follow-up visit at least every 60 days; at least two in-person visits a year, with the rest allowed by phone or video. Visits are documented.

citations.title: ODA personal care: policies and service verification
citations.requirement: Written policies on job descriptions and on records showing each PCA's qualifications. Per episode, keep date, arrival and departure times, activities, PCA name and ID, and client ID. Subject to Chapter 5160-32 EVV and ORC 121.36.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: scope and medication
citations.requirement: Services follow the PCSP and are limited to the approved hours. Aides do not administer prescribed or OTC medications. They may only help with self-administration: remind, hand the container, open it, assist the physically impaired.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: provider and aide requirements
citations.requirement: Agency aides must be employed by a Medicare-certified or accredited agency. They need an ODH/Medicare competency certificate, first aid, 8 in-service hours a year, and RN/LPN home visits every 60 days. Non-agency aides complete 6 in-service hours.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver personal care aide: clinical record
citations.requirement: Confidential clinical record at the place of business. Contents: ID data, PCSP, allergies and dietary restrictions, advance directives, task log with times and dated signatures, signed progress notes, and a discharge summary.

citations.title: ODM waiver provider conditions of participation
citations.requirement: Active Medicaid agreement; staff age 18+; written acknowledgment of 5160-44-05 on enrollment and yearly; new-provider training within 90 days; HIPAA and 42 CFR 431 compliance; contact updates within 7 days; back-up plan; 72-hour notice of planned absence.

citations.title: ODM waiver: visit documentation and retention
citations.requirement: Document each visit: tasks done or not done, date, location, start and end times, and provider and client signatures (client signature within 3 business days if not obtained at the visit). Keep service and billing records 6 years from payment or until audit ends.

citations.title: ODM waiver: 24-hour notices and termination of service
citations.requirement: Notify ODM or its designee within 24 hours of changes in client condition, environment, caregiver, move, refusals, threats, or safety concerns. Give 30 days' written notice before ending service (10 days after hospital, institution or jail).

citations.title: ODM waiver: EVV, prohibited conduct, legal decision-makers
citations.requirement: Personal care visits must be verified by ODM-approved EVV. Prohibits abuse, gifts or loans, falsifying signatures, billing while the client is hospitalized, sleeping, visitors, impairment, and acting as POA or guardian.

citations.title: HCBS waiver incident management
citations.requirement: Providers take immediate protective action and report any incident to the case management agency immediately, and no later than 1 business day. Defines critical incidents (abuse, neglect, exploitation, medication error, death, missing) and required report contents.

citations.title: Person-centered planning (HCBS)
citations.requirement: The individual leads planning. The service plan must be in plain language, accessible to LEP and disabled persons, signed, and distributed. It includes back-up plans and is reviewed at least every 12 months, on significant change, or on request.

citations.title: Older Americans Act: personal care
citations.requirement: Staffing adequate for personal care at least 5 days a week. Back-up plan when no aide is available. Supervisor available during scheduled hours. Aide qualifications and 6 hours of ODA-approved in-service per 12 months.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver billing and covered services
citations.requirement: Sets billing and reimbursement for Ohio Home Care Waiver services, including personal care aide units. Read the current text (effective Apr 17, 2026) before billing.

citations.title: Ohio Home Care Waiver: home care attendant
citations.requirement: Home care attendant service (S5125) rate and billing rules; includes nursing-task component outside nonmedical scope. Applies only if the agency enrolls for that service.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care aide service (EVV-covered, T1019)
citations.requirement: Personal care aide service under HCPCS T1019 is subject to Electronic Visit Verification. Per ODM, EVV captures service type, recipient, date, location, worker and start/end time.

citations.title: PASSPORT eligibility and enrollment
citations.requirement: PASSPORT enrollment requires an open slot within the CMS-authorized limit. Providers accept referrals only for enrolled, authorized individuals.

citations.cite: Ohio Const. Art. II §34a; ORC Chapter 4111; Ohio Dept. of Commerce 2026 minimum wage notice
citations.title: Ohio minimum wage and poster
citations.requirement: 2026 Ohio minimum wage is $11.00/hour for non-tipped employees. It applies to employers above $405,000 gross receipts; smaller employers stay at the federal floor. Employers must display the official 2026 poster.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owners, officers, governing body, administrator, supervisors and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, who is accountable for compliance with Ohio law, and what ownership and registration information must be kept accurate and disclosed to ODH, ODA and ODM.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a nonmedical home health services provider. Under ORC 3740.02 it may provide, or hold itself out as providing, nonmedical home health services only while it holds a current license from the Ohio Department of Health (ODH). The services are home health aide services and personal care services, including help with self-administration, as defined in ORC 3740.01. The agency is governed by [GOVERNING BODY / OWNER NAME(S)], which holds final responsibility for legal compliance, finances, policies and quality. The governing body appoints an administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], who manages daily operations. The rules reviewed for this manual set no specific administrator qualifications. The agency therefore names the administrator in writing, sets its own minimum qualifications in the job description (PER-03), and confirms the standard with ODH in writing and keeps the reply on file. The agency discloses its owners and officers to ODH with the license application. If the agency is certified by the Ohio Department of Aging (ODA), it also discloses owners, any felony convictions of owners, and an organization table to ODA. It keeps an active Ohio Secretary of State registration at all times. If the agency is ODA-certified, it makes the attestations required by OAC 173-39-02(C)(1) and requires staff to meet the conduct standards in its written policies (PER-15).

definitions.definition: The owner(s), board or officers with legal authority over [AGENCY NAME] and final responsibility for its operation.
The person named by the governing body to manage daily operations and ensure compliance with this manual and applicable law.
Home health aide services and personal care services, including help with self-administration, as defined in ORC 3740.01. They exclude skilled or medical care.
A person with an ownership interest in, or an officer position in, the agency, as disclosed on the ODH application and, if certified, to ODA.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organization chart showing the governing body, administrator, supervisor(s) and caregivers, and reviews it at least annually or on any change in ownership or leadership.

The governing body appoints the administrator in writing and records the name, start date and contact information ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME], [PHONE]). It names a written alternate who acts when the administrator is unavailable.
Before appointment, the governing body sets the administrator's minimum qualifications in the job description (PER-03).

Within 30 days of appointing the administrator, the owner writes to ODH to confirm whether any administrator qualification standard applies. The agency files the request and ODH's reply in the governance file.

The administrator holds authority for hiring, supervision, scheduling, policy implementation, records, complaints, incidents and billing integrity, and reports compliance status to the governing body at least quarterly.
The administrator maintains a list of all owners and officers with names, titles, percentage of ownership and addresses. The list is updated within 10 days of any change.

For the ODH application, the owner submits fingerprints, Secretary of State filings, the notarized identity affidavit, the written criminal records check policy, days and hours, services and policies, service area, the surety bond and the fee as required by ORC 3740.03 (see GOV-02).

If the agency is ODA-certified, the administrator discloses all owners, any felony convictions of owners, and the organization table to ODA. The administrator keeps proof of an active Secretary of State registration.

If the agency is ODA-certified, the owner signs the attestations required under OAC 173-39-02(C)(1): compliance with 45 CFR 80.4, equal employment opportunity, wage and hour law and workers' compensation, and payment of taxes. The administrator verifies each item before signing and keeps supporting proof.
The administrator checks the Secretary of State registration status every quarter and files any required renewal or report before it is due.
The administrator reports any change in owners, officers, name, address, services or service area to ODH as required by GOV-07.
The administrator ensures every employee receives and signs for the conduct standards in PER-15, and that those standards cover the conduct expected under ODA and ODM rules.
The governing body reviews the QA report (GOV-05), complaints, incidents and any regulator correspondence at least quarterly. It records its decisions in dated minutes.
The administrator never allows services to be advertised or delivered before the ODH license is issued (GOV-02).

The administrator keeps governance records (organization chart, minutes, disclosures, attestations, SOS proof, ODH correspondence) at the business site (REC-03) and makes them available to regulators on request.

responsibilities.duty: Holds ultimate responsibility, appoints the administrator, signs filings and attestations, reviews quarterly compliance reports and keeps ownership information current.
Manages operations, confirms administrator standards with ODH, maintains disclosures and SOS registration, and ensures policies are followed.
Acts with the administrator's authority when the administrator is absent and documents decisions made.
Follow this manual and the conduct standards, and report compliance concerns to the administrator.

documentation: Organization chart with revision dates
Administrator appointment letter and alternate designation
Written request to ODH on administrator standards and ODH reply
Owner and officer list with change dates
Secretary of State registration proof and quarterly status check log
ODA owner, felony and organization table disclosures (if certified)
Signed ODA attestations (if certified)
Governing body minutes

policies.title: Licensure, Advertising and Surety Bond Requirements
policies.applies_to: Owners, administrator, anyone who markets, advertises or schedules services for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] provides and advertises services only while holding a current ODH nonmedical home health services license, keeps the required surety bond, and renews on time.
policies.policy: No services will be provided, offered or advertised until ODH has issued the nonmedical license (ORC 3740.02; OAC 3701-60-02). Operating or advertising without a license is a second-degree misdemeanor on a first offense and a first-degree misdemeanor for each later offense. The application is complete only with the prescribed forms, the $250 non-refundable fee, the owner and officer information, the services list and related policies, Secretary of State documents, the written criminal records check policy, hours of operation, service area, owner fingerprints, the notarized identity affidavit and the $20,000 surety bond from a surety licensed to do business in Ohio (ORC 3740.03(B); OAC 3701-60-03(B)). ODH reviews the application and issues the license once the fee is paid and the requirements are shown, unless ORC 3740.07 applies (ORC 3740.04). The license is valid for three years. Renewal requires the $250 renewal fee and a showing of continued compliance with ORC 3740.03 (ORC 3740.05). After issuance, the agency uses its exact licensed legal name in all materials and may state it is "licensed by the Ohio Department of Health". It does not use that statement before the license is issued.

definitions.definition: Any public statement that the agency provides or will provide nonmedical home health services, including websites, social media, directories, signs, flyers, referral-source presentations and online job postings that describe client services.
A $20,000 bond issued by a surety licensed to do business in Ohio, required of a new provider with the initial application.
The agency name exactly as it appears on the ODH license and Secretary of State registration.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the owner confirms the agency's legal name, address, owner and officer information and Secretary of State registration so they match across all filings.

The administrator assembles the application using ODH's prescribed forms: owner and officer information, services list and related policies (GOV-03), days and hours, service area, Secretary of State documents, notarized identity affidavit and the written criminal records check policy (PER-04 through PER-08).
Each owner completes fingerprinting as ODH directs. The administrator keeps the receipts.
The owner obtains the $20,000 surety bond from a surety licensed in Ohio before filing, and the administrator files a copy in the licensure file (see GOV-08).

The owner pays the $250 non-refundable fee by cashier's check or postal money order payable to "Treasurer, State of Ohio", or electronically through the ODH e-form. Mailed applications and payments go to ODH Revenue Processing #3506, P.O. Box 15278, Columbus OH 43215.
The administrator keeps a copy of the complete submission and proof of payment, and records the date filed.
If the agency is certified by ODA, the administrator checks ODH's current instructions on the waiver in ORC 3740.03(B)(3) and files for it only if ODH confirms eligibility.

The statute sets no day limit for ODH to issue the license. If ODH asks for more information, the administrator replies as quickly as possible and within any deadline ODH states. The administrator confirms any general status-inquiry timeframe with ODH directly.
No services are scheduled or accepted, and no clients are enrolled, until the license is in hand. The administrator records the license number, issue date and expiration date.

Before any advertisement or marketing item is published, the administrator reviews it and confirms that the licensed legal name is used. The administrator confirms that the license statement appears only after issuance, and that the item describes only services allowed under ORC 3740.01 (see SVC-01).
The administrator keeps a log of every public advertisement with date, medium and the approving signature. If any pre-license content appears online, the administrator removes it immediately.
The administrator posts or keeps the license at the business site where regulators and clients can see it, and provides a copy to clients on request.

The administrator calendars the license expiration date. The administrator confirms the renewal filing deadline with ODH in writing, and starts the renewal at least 120 days before expiration (agency policy).

To renew, the administrator pays the $250 renewal fee and assembles proof of continued compliance with ORC 3740.03 requirements, including current ownership information and the surety bond (see GOV-07). The administrator keeps a copy of the filing and proof of payment.
The agency keeps the surety bond in force as ODH requires. The administrator contacts the surety each year to confirm the bond is active and keeps the confirmation.

If the license lapses, expires or is suspended or revoked, the administrator immediately stops all services and advertising and notifies the governing body, ODH, clients and any Medicaid case management agency or payer so that care can transfer safely (SVC-11).

responsibilities.duty: Signs the application, pays fees, obtains the bond and is fingerprinted.
Prepares filings, approves advertising, tracks renewal and bond dates and stops services if the license is not current.
Use only approved materials and the licensed legal name, and refuse to accept clients before licensure.

documentation: Complete ODH application copy and fee payment proof
Surety bond and annual surety confirmation
ODH license and expiration calendar
ODH correspondence on application status and information requests
Advertising approval log
Renewal filing and fee proof

policies.title: Services List, Days and Hours of Operation and Geographic Service Area
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors, intake and scheduling staff and caregivers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To state the services [AGENCY NAME] provides, when it operates, and where it serves clients, as the ODH application requires, and to keep these statements current and consistent with practice.
policies.policy: The ODH application must contain a list of the nonmedical services provided and the related policies and procedures, a statement of the days and hours of operation, and a description of the geographic area served (ORC 3740.03(B); OAC 3701-60-03(B)). This policy meets OAC 3701-60-03(B)(3)(h) — statement of days and hours of operation, and OAC 3701-60-03(B)(3)(i) — description of the geographic area to be served. It also meets item B(3)(d) — last day of service: the agency gives the individual and ODA's designee at least thirty days' written notice before the last day of service, except in the circumstances the rule lists (see SVC-11). Services are limited to the nonmedical scope of ORC 3740.01: personal care and home health aide services, including help with self-administration. The agency provides no skilled or medical services. Days and hours of operation: [DAYS AND HOURS OF OPERATION, including how clients reach the agency after hours at [PHONE]]. Geographic area served: [COUNTIES / CITIES / ZIP CODES SERVED]. The current statements are kept as an appendix to this manual and are updated whenever they change.

definitions.definition: The written list of nonmedical services [AGENCY NAME] offers, each tied to a policy in this manual.
The days and hours the business office is staffed and when client services are scheduled, including after-hours contact arrangements.
The counties, cities or ZIP codes in which the agency accepts clients and sends caregivers.
The final day the agency provides services to a client for any reason, including discharge or discontinuation.

procedures: The administrator maintains the Services List appendix. It lists each service offered (such as bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting and incontinence care, mobility and transfer help, meal preparation, light housekeeping, laundry, companionship and reminders or help with self-administration as ORC 3740.01 permits). Each service is cross-referenced to SVC-01 and SVC-06.
The administrator confirms before any service is added that it falls inside the nonmedical scope of ORC 3740.01. The administrator rejects any skilled or medical task, and documents the review.
The administrator confirms that a written policy and procedure exists for each listed service and attaches the list with those policies to the ODH application.

The administrator records the Days and Hours of Operation statement in the appendix, including holidays, any 24-hour or weekend scheduling and the after-hours telephone number. The statement is included in the ODH application and is identical to what is given to clients (CR-06).
The administrator records the Geographic Service Area statement in the appendix, listing each county or area by name, and shows it on a map in the licensure file.
The administrator reviews the three statements at least annually, and whenever the agency adds or removes a service, changes its hours, or expands or reduces its area.

Before any change takes effect, the administrator updates the appendix, notifies ODH under GOV-07 when ODH requires it, and informs affected clients, caregivers and any Medicaid case management agency.

Intake staff screen each referral against the service area and services list (SVC-02). They decline, in writing, any referral outside the area or needing services the agency does not provide, and they offer referral information to another provider.

Scheduling staff assign caregivers only within the stated service area and hours, unless the administrator documents an approved exception. Care outside the stated hours is not scheduled without the administrator's approval.

To close or discontinue services to a client, the administrator follows SVC-11. Except in the circumstances the rule lists, the administrator gives the client and, for Medicaid program clients, ODA's designee written notice at least thirty days before the last day of service (item B(3)(d)). The administrator documents the notice date, the reason and how it was delivered.
If a listed exception applies and less than thirty days' notice is given, the administrator records the exception relied upon and notifies the client and ODA's designee as soon as possible.
The administrator keeps dated copies of every version of the services list, hours statement and service area description for audit and renewal.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the three statements, approves changes, notifies ODH and ensures notice-of-last-service requirements are met.
Screen referrals and schedule only within the stated services, hours and area.
Confirms the service plan stays within the listed services and reports any request for services outside the list.

documentation: Services List appendix with version dates
Days and Hours of Operation statement
Geographic Service Area description and map
Referral decline letters
Thirty-day last-day-of-service notices and any recorded exceptions
Notices to ODH of changes

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors and all staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure written policies are developed, implemented, followed and maintained, kept current with changes in Ohio rules, and acknowledged by every staff member.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5) — Provider policies: [AGENCY NAME] develops, implements, complies with and maintains written or electronic policies on all required topics. For the ODA personal care rule these include written policies on job descriptions (PER-03) and on records showing each personal care aide's qualifications (PER-02). The agency also keeps written policies requiring staff to meet the conduct standards ODA sets for certified providers (PER-15). The administrator reviews the entire manual at least annually and whenever a rule, program requirement or agency practice changes. The agency subscribes to ODA's rule-update emails and monitors OAC Chapter 3701-60, which is next due for five-year review on 01/27/2028. Every revision carries a version number and date, and every employee signs an acknowledgment of the policies that apply to the job.

definitions.definition: A policy, procedure, form or appendix with a version number, effective date and approver, kept in the master manual.
A documented check that a policy matches current law and actual practice, resulting in either 'no change' or a revision.
A signed and dated record that an employee received, read and agrees to follow specified policies.

procedures: The administrator keeps the master copy of the manual, in paper or electronic form, with every policy showing its ID, title, version number, effective date and approver. Only the administrator may change the master copy.
The administrator assigns each policy an owner (administrator, supervisor or other designated person) responsible for its accuracy.

The administrator confirms that written policies exist and are in the manual for each topic in OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5): job descriptions (PER-03) and PCA qualification records (PER-02). The administrator verifies this against the current rule text at each annual review.

The administrator subscribes at least one monitored agency email address to ODA's rule-update notices, and checks the Ohio Administrative Code for Chapter 3701-60 and other applicable rules at least quarterly.

When a rule change is announced, the administrator logs the date and a summary, and within 30 days decides which policies must change. If the rule has an earlier effective date, the policy change is completed before that date.

The administrator completes a full annual review of every policy, no later than 12 months after the previous review. Reviewers record 'no change' or the revision made, with name and date, on the Policy Review Log.

Policy changes are drafted by the policy owner, approved in writing by the administrator, and where the change affects governance or ownership, by the governing body. The version number increases and the old version is archived, not discarded.
Within 14 days of any approved change, the administrator distributes the revised policy to the affected staff, trains them on it where needed and collects a signed acknowledgment.
Each new employee receives the manual sections relevant to the job at orientation (PER-09) and signs an acknowledgment before working alone with a client.
Supervisors observe whether the policies are actually followed during supervisory visits and chart audits. Gaps are reported to the administrator and handled under GOV-05.
The administrator keeps the archived versions, the Policy Review Log, the rule-update log and all acknowledgments for at least 6 years, or longer if another policy sets a longer period (REC-01).
If a regulator requests a policy, the administrator provides the current approved version and the revision history promptly (REC-03).

responsibilities.duty: Controls the master manual, runs the annual review, monitors rule changes, approves revisions and ensures acknowledgments.
Draft accurate revisions and confirm the policy matches actual practice.
Train caregivers on changes and report practice that departs from policy.
Read, follow and acknowledge the policies applicable to the job.

documentation: Master manual with version numbers and dates
Policy Review Log
Rule-update log and ODA email subscription confirmation
Archived prior versions
Signed staff acknowledgments
Staff training records on policy changes

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors and quality reviewers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To monitor on a regular schedule whether the agency is meeting its policies and Ohio requirements, to find problems early, and to correct them in a documented way.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality assurance and performance improvement (QAPI) program. The administrator audits records monthly, covering criminal records and database screening status, in-service hours, supervisory visits, EVV and visit records, and incident reports. The audited visit records reflect what OAC 173-39-02.11(C)(5)-(6) requires for service verification: date, arrival and departure times, activities, caregiver name and ID, and client ID. Incident review reflects the immediate protective action and reporting to the case management agency required by OAC 5160-44-05. The agency also tracks missed visits, complaints, incidents and abuse, neglect and exploitation reports, and reviews them with the administrator. Corrective actions are documented and closed within 30 days. The monthly audit frequency and the 30-day close-out period are agency policy, not rule requirements.

definitions.definition: The agency's planned process for measuring performance, identifying problems, correcting them and checking that the corrections worked.
A documented step that fixes a finding and prevents it from happening again, with an owner and due date.
A measurable item reviewed regularly, such as percentage of supervisory visits completed on time.

procedures: By the 10th of each month, the administrator audits the prior month for these indicators: (a) criminal records check and database screening status for every caregiver (PER-04 to PER-08); (b) in-service training hours (PER-11); (c) supervisory visits completed on schedule (SVC-04); (d) EVV and visit records complete and matching the schedule and billing (SVC-09); and (e) incident reports (SAF-02).

The administrator reviews a sample of at least [NUMBER] client records per month, or all records if the agency has fewer. The review confirms that service plans, visit documentation and signatures are complete and consistent with the plan.

The administrator compares each visit record with the elements required: date, location, arrival and departure times, tasks done or not done, caregiver name and ID, client ID and required signatures. Gaps are flagged for follow-up.
The administrator keeps a running log of missed and late visits (SVC-07), complaints (CR-02), incidents (SAF-02) and abuse, neglect or exploitation reports (SAF-01), with dates, causes and outcomes.

The administrator confirms that every incident involved immediate protective action and was reported to the case management agency immediately and no later than 1 business day, where a waiver client was involved (SAF-02, SVC-14).
Each finding is entered on a Corrective Action Plan with the problem, root cause, action, responsible person and due date. The due date is no later than 30 days after the finding.

The responsible person completes the action, records the date and evidence, and the administrator verifies the fix. For issues that threaten client safety, the administrator acts immediately without waiting for the monthly cycle.
If a corrective action cannot be closed within 30 days, the administrator records the reason, the new date and interim safeguards, and informs the governing body.
For problems that recur, the administrator analyzes causes (for example, scheduling, training or supervision gaps) and changes the policy, training or staffing as needed (GOV-04).
The administrator prepares a written QA summary each quarter with indicator results, trends, open corrective actions and recommendations, and presents it to the governing body (GOV-01).
Staff may report quality concerns to the administrator at any time without retaliation. Reports are logged and reviewed in the next monthly audit.
QA documents are kept at least 6 years and are available to regulators (REC-01, REC-03). They contain client information, so access is limited to those who need it (CR-03).

responsibilities.duty: Performs the monthly audit, maintains logs, assigns and verifies corrective actions and reports quarterly to the governing body.
Supply supervisory-visit data, resolve findings assigned to them and report trends from the field.
Reviews QA summaries and provides resources for improvement.

documentation: Monthly QA audit checklist and results
Logs of missed visits, complaints, incidents and abuse/neglect reports
Corrective Action Plans with closure dates
Quarterly QA summary and governing body minutes

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Owners, administrator, billing staff, supervisors and caregivers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To prevent fraud, waste and improper billing, and to make sure all claims to Medicaid and ODA programs are supported by complete, truthful records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered, as authorized and as documented. The agency accepts the agreed rate as payment in full from Medicaid and ODA programs (OAC 173-39-02(B)). It never bills for a client who is hospitalized. It never falsifies client signatures or visit times, and it never accepts gifts or loans from clients. It does not allow staff to act as a client's power of attorney or guardian while delivering services (OAC 5160-44-31). Personal care visits for Ohio Home Care Waiver clients are verified by ODM-approved EVV. Visit documentation shows tasks done or not done, date, location, start and end times, and signatures. A client signature that was not obtained at the visit is obtained within 3 business days. The agency cooperates with ODM monitoring and reviews and gives ODA, ODM, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the Auditor of State immediate access to records. ODM is increasing payment suspensions and program-integrity actions, so the agency keeps complete time, EVV, supervision and screening records. Before any Medicaid enrollment, the administrator checks ODM's current enrollment and moratorium status. ODM paused new Medicaid enrollment for home health, hospice and related provider types from May 14, 2026 through Nov 14, 2026, and whether personal care aide and home care attendant provider types are covered has not been confirmed. The administrator confirms this with ODM before applying.

definitions.definition: Knowingly submitting or causing a false claim or record, such as billing for services not delivered or altering time records.
The agreed Medicaid or ODA rate is the entire payment. The agency does not bill the client or family for any difference.
A temporary hold on Medicaid payments by ODM, typically on credible allegation of fraud or another program-integrity finding.
Electronic visit verification, an ODM-approved system that records the caregiver's arrival and departure and the service delivered.

procedures: The administrator designates a compliance contact (the administrator unless the governing body names another person). Staff may report concerns to that person, or directly to the governing body, without retaliation.
At hire and annually, every employee receives training on this policy, the prohibitions listed above and how to report suspected fraud. Each employee signs an acknowledgment (PER-09, PER-11).

Billing staff bill only from verified visit records. Before submission, they compare each claim with the authorized service plan, the EVV record and the visit documentation, and resolve any mismatch first.

Staff must record actual start and end times. No one may alter, estimate or back-fill visit times or tasks. Any correction is made by a dated, signed addendum that explains the change, never by overwriting.

No one may sign for a client or obtain a client's signature by deception. If the client's signature was not obtained at the visit, the supervisor obtains it within 3 business days and records the date (SVC-09).

Scheduling or billing staff verify hospital admission status. When the agency learns a client is hospitalized, the administrator suspends service and billing for those dates immediately and documents the date.

The agency never bills for time when a caregiver was sleeping, impaired, had visitors present, or otherwise not delivering the authorized services. Supervisors address any such report right away under PER-15.

Caregivers may not accept gifts or loans from clients, or act as a client's power of attorney or guardian (CR-04). The administrator reviews any report of a breach and may suspend the employee during review.

The agency accepts the agreed Medicaid or ODA rate as payment in full. It does not charge Medicaid or PASSPORT clients any additional amount for covered services. Any private-pay rate is stated in the service agreement (CR-06).
Each month the administrator completes a billing integrity check as part of GOV-05: a sample of claims matched to visit records, EVV data and caregiver screening and training status.

Before applying for Medicaid enrollment, the administrator checks ODM's current moratorium notice and confirms with ODM in writing, through the ODM Integrated Help Desk at 1-800-686-1516, whether the personal care aide and home care attendant provider types are covered. The agency starts no billing before enrollment is complete and approved.

If a payment suspension, audit, records request or review notice arrives, the administrator notifies the governing body the same day, assembles the requested records and gives auditors immediate access. The administrator consults legal counsel when advisable.

If the agency finds that it was overpaid or billed incorrectly, the administrator stops further billing for the item, corrects the claim and refunds or adjusts as the payer directs. The administrator documents the correction and cause, and consults counsel on whether and how to report to the payer.

The administrator keeps service and billing records at least 6 years after payment, or until any review or audit ends, whichever is later, and keeps qualification records for the period of employment plus 6 years (REC-01).
The agency does not retaliate against anyone who reports a compliance concern in good faith. Retaliation is grounds for discipline up to termination.

responsibilities.duty: Sets a culture of compliance, receives reports and supports corrective action.
Runs training and monthly billing checks, responds to audits and suspensions, and confirms enrollment status with ODM.
Submit only supported claims and flag mismatches before billing.
Verify visit records and signatures and report suspected falsification.
Document truthfully, use EVV correctly and follow the prohibited-conduct rules.

documentation: Compliance training records and signed acknowledgments
Monthly billing integrity check results
EVV records matched to claims
Hospitalization suspension notes
Client signature follow-up records
Reports of suspected fraud and outcomes
ODM enrollment and moratorium status confirmation
Audit, review and payment suspension correspondence
Overpayment and refund records

policies.title: ODH License Renewal, Change Notices and Enforcement
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body, and any staff member who receives mail, e-mail or calls from the Ohio Department of Health (ODH)
policies.purpose: To keep the nonmedical home health services license in good standing by renewing on time, telling ODH about changes within 10 days, answering ODH requests within 14 days, and responding correctly to any enforcement action.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will keep its ODH nonmedical home health services license in good standing at all times. The license is valid for three years (ORC 3740.05; OAC 3701-60-03). The agency will file its renewal application and the $250 renewal fee at least 90 days before the license expires, so that the renewal is timely under OAC 3701-60-03, and will show continued compliance with ORC 3740.03. The agency will give ODH written notice within 10 days of any change to the information in its application, including the owner, address, agency name, services, days and hours, geographic service area, and surety bond. The agency will reply to every ODH information request within 14 days of the mailing date. [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] is the one named person who sends notices to ODH and keeps proof of delivery. ODH may refuse to issue or renew a license, or may limit, suspend or revoke it, or impose probation or a reprimand (ORC 3740.07). The Director may deny, suspend or revoke a license for material misrepresentation, failure to timely renew, or no longer meeting requirements (OAC 3701-60-04). The agency will respond to any such action through the hearing process of ORC Chapter 119 and will use informal dispute resolution when it is available after a denial. This policy meets official checklist item I (OAC 3701-60-06(I)): the agency applies the exception for applicants referred by an employment service only as described in PER-07. That is, a new check is not requested only if the employment service confirms in writing that it completed the database review and a criminal records check within the past year and both reports show no disqualifying offense. The agency keeps that documentation so it can show continued compliance at renewal and on any ODH request.

definitions.definition: Any change to information given to ODH in the license application, such as owner, address, name, services, days and hours, service area, or surety bond.
A renewal application filed with ODH at least 90 days before the license expiration date (OAC 3701-60-03).

The exception in OAC 3701-60-06(I) under which the agency need not request its own criminal records check on an applicant referred by an employment service when the service confirms a database review and a criminal records check within one year and both reports show no disqualifying offense.
A refusal to issue or renew, limitation, suspension, revocation, probation or reprimand imposed by ODH under ORC 3740.07 and OAC 3701-60-04.

procedures: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] is the designated notice person. A back-up person named by the governing body acts when the Administrator is absent. Both names are recorded in the Regulatory Calendar.

On receipt of the license, the Administrator records the issue date and expiration date in the Regulatory Calendar and on the agency's shared electronic calendar. The Administrator confirms the dates against the license document itself and against any ODH letter adjusting the renewal date (ORC 3740.05).

The Administrator sets calendar reminders at 180, 120 and 90 days before expiration. The 120-day reminder starts the renewal packet. The 90-day date is the last day a renewal can be filed and still be timely.

At the 120-day reminder, the Administrator reviews the application on file against current operations (owner, address, services, hours, service area, policies, bond) and corrects any difference through the change-notice process in steps 8-10 before renewal is filed.

At the 120-day reminder, the Administrator also confirms that the $20,000 surety bond is in force (GOV-08), that the criminal records check policy is current (PER-04), and that the employment-service exception records are complete (see step 7).

The Administrator prepares the renewal application and the $250 renewal fee, files them with ODH by the method ODH currently accepts, and files no later than 90 days before expiration. The Administrator keeps a copy of the filing, the payment record and proof of delivery.

Employment-service exception (checklist item I, OAC 3701-60-06(I)): the Administrator or hiring designee uses the exception only under PER-07. Before relying on it, the designee obtains the employment service's written confirmation of the database review and the criminal records check, the dates of both (within one year), and a statement that neither report shows a disqualifying offense. The designee files the confirmation in the personnel record (PER-13). The Administrator audits these files before each renewal and removes the exception for any applicant whose paperwork is incomplete.

Within 10 days of any change to application information, the Administrator sends ODH written notice of the change. Examples are a new owner or ownership percentage, new business address, name change, added or dropped service, new days or hours, changed service area, and a new or replaced surety bond. The notice states what changed and the effective date.

The Administrator keeps a copy of each notice and proof of delivery (certified mail receipt, e-mail confirmation or portal receipt) in the Licensure File. The 10-day count starts on the date the change takes effect or is decided, whichever is earlier.
Any staff member who learns of a planned or actual change in the items above tells the Administrator the same day so the 10-day deadline can be met.

When any ODH letter, e-mail or call requesting information arrives, the receiving staff member gives it to the Administrator the same business day. The Administrator logs the mailing date and calculates the due date as 14 days from the mailing date.

The Administrator sends a complete written reply on or before the 14th day and keeps proof of delivery. If a complete reply cannot be assembled, the Administrator sends what is available before the deadline and states in writing when the rest will follow.

When ODH issues a notice of proposed denial, limitation, suspension, revocation, probation or reprimand, the Administrator gives it to the governing body the same day and calendars the response deadline stated in the notice.

The governing body decides within the notice period whether to request a hearing under ORC Chapter 119 and, after a denial, whether to use informal dispute resolution. The Administrator files the request in writing within the time stated in the notice and gets counsel involved as needed.

While an enforcement action is pending, the agency continues to meet all license requirements. If a suspension or revocation takes effect, the Administrator carries out the client transition steps in SVC-11 and notifies Medicaid payers and case management agencies (SVC-12).
After any ODH inspection, request or action, the Administrator reports findings and corrective steps to the governing body at its next meeting and enters them in the Quality Assurance log (GOV-05).
The Administrator reviews this policy and the Regulatory Calendar each year under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Serve as the sole sender of ODH notices; calendar and file the renewal at least 90 days before expiration; send 10-day change notices; answer ODH requests within 14 days; keep proof of delivery.
Approve the renewal filing, receive notice of any enforcement action the same day, and decide on hearing or informal dispute resolution requests.
Obtain and file employment-service confirmations before the exception in OAC 3701-60-06(I) is used.
Forward any ODH communication to the Administrator the same business day and report any change affecting the application.

documentation: Licensure File with the license, renewal packet, fee payment record and proof of filing
Regulatory Calendar with reminders at 180, 120 and 90 days
Copies of 10-day change notices with proof of delivery
ODH request log with mailing date, due date, reply date and proof of delivery
Enforcement action file, including notices, hearing requests and correspondence
Employment-service confirmations filed in personnel records

policies.title: Insurance, Surety Bond and Theft or Property Damage Loss Claims
policies.applies_to: Administrator, intake staff, supervisors and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure the agency keeps required insurance and the surety bond in force and that every client knows, in writing, how to obtain payment for loss caused by theft or property damage by the agency or its employees.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will keep the $20,000 surety bond required for its ODH nonmedical home health services license continuously in force (ORC 3740.03(B)). For services delivered as an ODA-certified provider, the agency will also carry $1,000,000 in commercial liability insurance that covers theft and property damage (OAC 173-39-02(A)). This policy meets OAC 173-39-02(A)(5)(b): the agency gives every individual written instructions that the individual may use to obtain payment for loss due to theft or property damage caused by the agency or by an agency employee. The instructions are handed out at intake, and the agency keeps a signed receipt. The agency does not discourage or delay any claim, and clients may also contact the police, their case management agency, ODA, ODM, or ODH.

definitions.definition: A $20,000 bond issued by a surety licensed to do business in Ohio, filed with the ODH license application.
A request by a client or the client's representative for payment for loss due to theft or property damage by the agency or an agency employee.
The written handout that explains how an individual obtains payment for such loss, as required by OAC 173-39-02(A)(5)(b).

procedures: Before the license application is filed and at each renewal, the Administrator obtains the surety bond and places a copy in the Licensure File. The Administrator calendars the bond renewal and any cancellation notice period 60 days ahead of its end date.

The Administrator keeps the commercial liability policy in force at no less than $1,000,000, confirms with the insurer in writing that it covers theft and property damage by employees, and files the certificate of insurance.

The Administrator prepares the Loss Claim Instructions handout. It states in plain language: (a) the individual may report a loss to the agency orally or in writing at [PHONE] or [ADDRESS]; (b) the agency will give a claim form on request and will help complete it; (c) the agency will notify its insurer and bond company of the claim; (d) the individual may also report to law enforcement; (e) the individual may contact the case management agency, ODA at 1-800-266-4346, or ODM Integrated Help Desk at 1-800-686-1516; (f) the agency's insurer and claim contact are [INSURER NAME AND CLAIMS PHONE].
The handout is offered in other languages and accessible formats on request (CR-05).
At intake, the intake staff member gives each client or the client's representative a copy of the Loss Claim Instructions and reviews them aloud or in the client's preferred format.

The client or representative signs a receipt for the instructions. If the client refuses to sign, the staff member notes the refusal and the date on the receipt form and leaves the handout with the client.
The signed receipt is filed in the client record (REC-01) within 2 business days of intake.
The handout is given again whenever the instructions change, and on request at any time.
A caregiver who is told of a possible theft or damage, or who notices a missing item, reports it to the supervisor the same day. The caregiver never confronts the client or a family member.
The supervisor notifies the Administrator the same day. The Administrator opens an incident report under SAF-02 and, if exploitation is suspected, follows SAF-01 and CR-04.
The Administrator acknowledges any loss claim in writing, tells the client what will happen next, and sends notice to the insurer and, where the bond may apply, to the surety.

The Administrator investigates by interviewing involved staff, reviewing schedules and EVV visit records (SVC-09), and reviewing prior incidents. The Administrator suspends a caregiver from the client's home while the allegation is investigated and does not retaliate against a client who files a claim.
The Administrator records the claim outcome and informs the client in writing. If the agency or the insurer denies the claim, the letter states the client's other options in the handout (step 3).
The Administrator reports claim trends to the governing body each quarter (GOV-05) and reports substantiated theft to the payer or case management agency as required (SVC-12, SVC-14, REC-02).
The Administrator reviews the bond and insurance each year and at each license renewal (GOV-07), and notifies ODH of a changed bond within 10 days.

responsibilities.duty: Maintain the bond and insurance, prepare and update the handout, manage loss claims and notify insurer and surety.
Hand out the instructions, explain them, and obtain and file the signed receipt.
Take same-day reports of loss or damage and escalate to the Administrator.
Report any loss or damage immediately and never confront the client or family.
Make sure funds are available to keep the bond and insurance active.

documentation: Surety bond and renewal/cancellation notices
Certificate of commercial liability insurance showing $1,000,000 and theft/property damage coverage
Loss Claim Instructions handout (current and prior versions)
Signed receipt of the instructions in each client record
Loss claim file with claim form, investigation, insurer correspondence and outcome
Incident report cross-reference

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All staff; clients and their representatives
policies.purpose: To make sure each client knows his or her rights, leads the planning of services, and is treated with dignity, privacy and choice in the home.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects the right of every client to lead the planning of his or her own services and to make choices about them (OAC 5160-44-02). For Medicaid home and community-based services clients, the agency follows 42 CFR 441.301(c) and supports the client's choice, privacy and dignity in the home setting. Written rights are given in plain language, in other languages and in accessible formats. A statement of rights is given at intake and the client or representative signs an acknowledgment. No staff member may deny, reduce or retaliate over the exercise of a right.

definitions.definition: Person-centered planning in which the individual directs the process and decides what matters in his or her services.
A person with legal authority to act for the client, such as a guardian or an agent under a power of attorney. Agency staff may not serve in this role for a client.
Large print, plain language, interpreter, translated text or other means that allows a person with limited English proficiency or a disability to understand.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written Client Rights and Responsibilities statement in plain language. The statement covers the rights listed in step 2 and the responsibilities in step 3.

Rights include: to be treated with dignity and respect; to lead planning and make choices about services; to have privacy and confidentiality (CR-03); to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation and retaliation (SAF-01); to refuse services; to know the services, schedule and any charges (CR-06); to receive services without discrimination (CR-05); to be told of changes to the plan; to file a grievance (CR-02); to receive loss-claim instructions (GOV-08); to have a caregiver who is qualified and identified by name; and to contact the case management agency, ODA, ODM or ODH.

Responsibilities include: giving accurate information; telling the agency of changes in health, address, schedule or hospitalization; providing a safe home; treating caregivers with respect; and notifying the agency promptly if a visit must be cancelled.

At intake (SVC-02), the intake staff member gives the statement to the client or representative and reviews it aloud or in the client's preferred format. Interpreter and translation services are used when needed (CR-05).
The client or representative signs a written acknowledgment. The staff member gives the client a copy and files the original in the client record within 2 business days.
The intake staff member makes sure the client is told that he or she, not the agency, leads the planning of services and may bring family, friends or an advocate to planning meetings.

The service plan (SVC-03) is written in plain language, reflects the client's own goals and choices, is signed, and a copy is given to the client. It is reviewed at least every 12 months, on a significant change, or on request.

Caregivers honor the client's choices about how tasks are done within the service plan and scope (SVC-01), knock before entering when appropriate, respect personal and household privacy, and explain what they are doing before providing personal care.

If a client's choice would create a risk to health or safety, the supervisor discusses the risk with the client, records the discussion, and notifies the case management agency (SVC-14) rather than overriding the choice.
If a client lacks capacity, the supervisor works with the legal decision-maker. No agency staff member may act as the client's power of attorney or guardian.
Any staff member who sees or hears of a right being violated reports it to the supervisor the same day. The Administrator handles it under CR-02 or SAF-01 as appropriate.
The Administrator re-gives the rights statement whenever it changes, when the client's representative changes, and at each annual plan review.
Staff are trained on client rights at orientation and in annual in-service (PER-09, PER-11).
The Administrator reviews client rights complaints and acknowledgment completion each quarter (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Maintain the rights statement, translations and accessible formats; review compliance quarterly.
Give and explain the statement and obtain the signed acknowledgment.
Support client-led planning, resolve rights concerns and document discussions on risky choices.
Honor client choices, privacy and dignity and report any suspected rights violation.

documentation: Client Rights and Responsibilities statement (all versions and translations)
Signed acknowledgment in each client record
Service plan showing client goals and choices
Notes of risk discussions and any notices to the case management agency
Training records on client rights

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All staff, clients, representatives and families
policies.purpose: To give clients an easy, safe way to raise complaints and to make sure every complaint is acknowledged, investigated, resolved and recorded.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] accepts complaints from clients, representatives and families orally or in writing, and does not retaliate against anyone who complains.
