The agency gives ODH written notice within 10 days of any change in its license application information. The agency replies to ODH information requests within 14 days of mailing. A renewal is timely if filed at least 90 days before expiration of the 3-year license (OAC 3701-60-03(G)-(J)). Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported to Adult Protective Services, and ODA or its designee is notified, within 1 business day. Significant changes affecting a PASSPORT client are reported within 1 business day. The agency gives 30 days' written notice before ending service, with the exceptions allowed under OAC 173-39-02(B)(3), and gives ODM 72 hours' notice of planned absences where required for waiver services. Item I, the employment-service exception, does not create a report. It is a record the agency must be able to show: the agency does not need to request its own criminal records check on an applicant referred by an employment service only if the service confirms that the database review and a criminal records check were completed within one year, and both reports show no disqualifying offense. The agency keeps that confirmation on file and applies PER-07 for procedures.

definitions.definition: The entity ODA authorizes to receive notices on its behalf, such as the Area Agency on Aging or PASSPORT Administrative Agency.
Monday through Friday, excluding state holidays.
The agency's log of recurring and event-driven reporting deadlines, with owners and proof of delivery.
A service that refers job applicants to employers and that has completed a database review and criminal records check before referral.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a reporting calendar that lists each report, who receives it, the deadline, the person responsible and the proof of delivery. The calendar is reviewed each month.

Contact changes: Within 7 days of any change in the agency's telephone number, mailing address or email address, the Administrator notifies ODA or its designee in writing and, at the same time, updates the information with ODM. The Administrator files the notice and the proof of delivery.

License application changes: Within 10 days of any change to information in the ODH application (for example, ownership, administrator, address or services), the Administrator sends ODH a written notice by a method that gives proof of delivery, and files it.

ODH information requests: When ODH sends a request, office staff log the date of mailing on the day it arrives. The Administrator sends a complete reply within 14 days of the mailing date and files the reply and proof of delivery.

Renewal: The Administrator calendars the license expiration date at the start of the 3-year term and starts the renewal at least 180 days before expiration. The Administrator files the renewal at least 90 days before expiration so that it is timely (see GOV-07).

Abuse, neglect and exploitation: Anyone who suspects it tells the Administrator or PCA Supervisor immediately. Within 1 business day, the Administrator reports to Adult Protective Services and notifies ODA or its designee, and records the date, time, person contacted and report number (see SAF-01).

Significant changes: When a PASSPORT client's condition, living situation or service needs change significantly, the PCA Supervisor tells the Administrator the same day. The Administrator sends the report to ODA or its designee within 1 business day (see SVC-14).

Ending service: Before the agency ends service to a client, the Administrator gives the client and ODA or its designee written notice at least 30 days in advance, unless an exception applies (such as immediate danger to the client or staff). The Administrator documents the exception relied on (see SVC-11).

Planned absences for waiver services: When a caregiver or the agency will be unavailable for a planned period, the Administrator gives the notice required under ODM rules, including 72 hours' notice for waiver services, and arranges the back-up plan (see SVC-08).

Employment-service exception (item I): When an applicant is referred by an employment service, the Administrator obtains the service's written confirmation of the database review and criminal records check, with the dates. The Administrator accepts the exception only if both were completed within the past year and both reports show no disqualifying offense.

If the employment-service confirmation is missing, older than one year, or shows a disqualifying offense, the Administrator does not use the exception and completes the agency's own check under PER-05 and PER-08 before hiring.
The Administrator files the employment-service confirmation in the applicant's personnel file (PER-13) and notes the date and the Administrator's review.
Staff keep proof of delivery for each report (dated email, fax confirmation, certified mail receipt or portal confirmation) with the copy of the report.

Each quarter, the Administrator checks the reporting calendar against the filed copies. The Administrator corrects any late or missing report and records the review in the quality assurance file (GOV-05).
Reports to the state contain only the information needed, in line with privacy rules (CR-03).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the reporting calendar, makes or approves all reports, keeps proof of delivery and applies the employment-service exception only with the required confirmation.
Tell the Administrator the same day of any suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or significant client change.
Log incoming regulator requests, track deadlines and file notices and proofs of delivery.

documentation: Reporting calendar
Contact change notices to ODA, its designee and ODM, with proof of delivery
ODH written change notices and replies to information requests
Abuse, neglect and exploitation report records
Significant change reports
Service-ending notices
Employment-service confirmations (item I)
Quarterly reporting review

policies.title: Business Site, Record Security and Regulator Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, office staff, PCA Supervisors and anyone who handles agency or client records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a business site with locked record storage, protects client information in every format, and gives regulators immediate access to records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a business site at [ADDRESS] with locked storage for records. The storage is accessible to ODA, ODM, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Auditor of State (OAC 173-39-02(A)). The agency gives ODA, ODM, HHS and the Auditor immediate access to its records on request (OAC 173-39-02(B)(10)-(13)) and also gives ODH access as its licensing rules require. The agency keeps a working email address and phone number on file with ODA or its designee. Electronic records are protected by access controls and backups in line with the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164). Only authorized staff may see client records, and only the information needed for the person's job.

definitions.definition: The physical location of the agency, where records are kept and available for regulator review.
Producing requested records when the regulator asks, during the visit, without delay.
Technical and administrative measures, such as unique user IDs, passwords and role-based permissions, that limit who can see or change records.
A representative of ODA, ODM, HHS, the Auditor of State or ODH with legal authority to review records.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a business site at [ADDRESS] that has locked cabinets or a locked room for client and personnel records, and posts the agency's phone number [PHONE].
Only the Administrator and designated staff hold keys or codes. The Administrator keeps a key log and changes locks or codes when a key holder leaves.
Paper records are kept in locked storage whenever the office is unattended. Staff do not leave records on desks, in vehicles or at home.
Records leave the business site only when needed for a visit or a regulator request. Staff log them out and in and keep them in a locked bag while transported.
Each electronic system uses unique user IDs and passwords. Staff do not share logins. Access is limited by role (for example, caregivers see only the assigned client's plan).
The Administrator removes a departing employee's system access and keys on the last day of employment and records it.
Workstations lock automatically after inactivity. Computers and devices holding client information use encryption and current security software.
The Administrator arranges automatic backups of electronic records at least daily to a secure location. The Administrator tests restoring a backup every quarter and records the result.
The Administrator keeps a current email address and phone number on file with ODA or its designee and ODM. Any change is reported within 7 days (REC-02).

When a regulator arrives or requests records, the first staff member present tells the Administrator or designee immediately. The staff member checks the representative's identification and the stated authority.

The Administrator or designee gives the regulator immediate access to the requested records, a private work area and, when asked, copies. The agency does not delay access to prepare records or ask the regulator to return later.
A staff member records the regulator's name, agency, date and time, records requested and records copied. The Administrator keeps copies of what was provided.
Records requested by mail, email or portal are sent to the regulator by a secure method.
A lost, stolen or improperly disclosed record is reported to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator follows CR-03 for privacy incident handling and SAF-02 for incident reporting.
The Administrator reviews physical and electronic security each year, including who has access, and corrects any gaps in writing.

required_items.text: A list of the nonmedical home health services which are or will be provided by the home health agency or nonagency provider and any policies and procedures related to those services, if applicable.
If the applicant for licensure is a home health agency, a copy of the home health agency's written criminal records check policy.
A statement identifying the days and hours of operation for the applicant.
A description of the geographic area to be served.

Written notice to the director within ten days of any change in the information given in the license application under (B)(3), or any other change that would make the submitted information inaccurate.
The chief administrator or designee requests that the superintendent conduct a criminal records check on each applicant for a direct care position.

The chief administrator or designee conducts a criminal background check on direct-care employees. For employees hired before 1/1/2008 it is no later than 30 days after the anniversary of the hire date and at least every five years. For employees hired on or after 1/1/2008 it is no later than 30 days after the fifth anniversary of the hire date and at least every five years.

Residency requirement: if the applicant cannot show five years of Ohio residency, or an FBI check within that period, the chief administrator requests that the superintendent obtain FBI information. The agency may request FBI information even if the applicant does meet the residency requirement.

Notification to the applicant or employee that fingerprint impressions are required and a criminal records check will be conducted. The notice must also cover any fee under (E)(2) and any fingerprinting fees authorized under ORC 109.572(C)(2).

Investigation fee: the agency pays BCI the prescribed fee for each check. It may charge the applicant a fee up to that amount only if it gives notice at the time of the initial application and Medicaid does not reimburse the fee.
Criminal records check forms: provide the prescribed forms and fingerprint impression sheet (or instructions), obtain the completed forms, and forward them to the superintendent.
An applicant or employee who fails to complete the forms or provide fingerprint impressions shall not be employed in any position for which a check is required.
Reverification of a criminal records check completed within the previous twelve months may be requested and accepted.

Exception: the agency need not request a check on an applicant referred by an employment service if the service confirms the database review and a criminal records check within one year, and both reports show no disqualifying offense.
Written instructions any individual may use to obtain payment for loss due to theft or property damage caused by the provider or the provider's employee.
Incident reporting: a written or electronic policy on documenting incidents that complies with paragraph (B)(3)(b) of the rule.

APS reporting: report any reasonable cause to believe an individual suffered abuse, neglect or exploitation to the local adult protective services program under ORC 5101.63. Also notify ODA or its designee within one business day.

Significant changes: notify ODA or its designee no later than one business day after becoming aware of a significant change affecting the individual's service needs or safety. The listed changes are (i) not providing an authorized service at the authorized time, (ii) the individual moving, (iii) repeated refusal of services, (iv) any incident subject to rule 5160-44-05, and (v) any other significant change in the individual's status or environment.
Notify ODA or its designee of any change in telephone number, mailing address or email address within seven days.
Last day of service: give the individual and ODA's designee written notice at least thirty days before the last day of service, except in the listed circumstances.
Confidentiality: the provider is subject to state and federal confidentiality laws (ORC 5160.45 to 5160.481, 42 CFR 431.300 to 431.307, 45 CFR parts 160, 162 and 164).
The provider shall supervise the provider's volunteers.

Ethical, professional, respectful and legal service standards: the provider shall not engage in unethical, unprofessional, disrespectful or illegal behavior. Items (a) to (n) cover alcohol, drugs, gifts and tips, sexual conduct, leaving the home, failing to cooperate with ODA, distracting activities, abuse or distress (including social media photos), personal relationships, decision-making roles, selling to or buying from the individual, use of the individual's food or property, taking the individual to the business site, and conflicts of interest.
Records retention: service records for six years after payment and until reviews and audits are resolved. Qualification records for the duration of certification or employment plus six years.

Policies: the agency provider shall have written policies, bylaws or articles of incorporation (or an electronic record of them) that include requirements for its employees to provide services in a manner compliant with paragraph (B)(8) of the rule.
Availability and staffing: accept a referral only if there are adequate staffing levels of PCAs and PCA supervisors to provide the hours authorized for each individual.
The PCA receives supervision from an RN or LPN under the direction of an RN during all hours PCAs are scheduled to work.
The provider shall maintain a back-up plan for providing personal care when no PCA or PCA supervisor is available.

PCA initial qualifications: (i) STNA, (ii) Medicare home health aide standards, (iii) previous experience, (iv) vocational programs, or (v) other programs with at least 30 hours of training covering the topics in (v)(b)(i)-(x).

Orientation before direct in-person contact. It must address (i) the provider's expectations of employees, (ii) ethical standards under rule 173-39-02, (iii) an overview of personnel policies, (iv) the organization and lines of communication of the agency, (v) incident-reporting procedures, (vi) emergency procedures, and (vii) standard precautions for infection control.
Additional training and competency evaluation if the PCA will perform activities for which the PCA was not trained or evaluated.
In-service training: each PCA completes six hours of ODA-approved in-service training every twelve months (ORC 173.525). Agency- and program-specific orientation do not count toward the six hours.

Verification of PCA qualifications: retain certificates of completion, or record the school or organization, course name, dates and hours. Also retain the nurse aide registry search results for STNAs and the previous-employment records for the experience pathway.
PCA supervisor qualifications: only an RN, or an LPN under the direction of an RN, may qualify as a PCA supervisor.

PCA supervisor visits: an initial in-person visit to define expected activities and develop a written or electronic activity plan. Subsequent visits are at least every sixty days, with provision for telephone or video visits if at least two in-person visits occur per year. Each visit is documented in the individual's record.
Provider policies: the provider shall develop, implement, comply with and maintain written or electronic policies on all of the following topics.
Job descriptions for each position.
Retaining records on how each PCA meets the qualifications in paragraph (C)(3) of the rule.

Service verification: for each episode retain (i) service date, (ii) PCA arrival time, (iii) PCA departure time, (iv) description of activities provided, (v) name of each PCA in contact with the individual, (vi) unique identifier of each PCA, and (vii) unique identifier of the individual. The provider is subject to Chapter 5160-32 (EVV) and ORC 121.36.

official.notes: No single ODH policy checklist or form exists for the nonmedical home health services license. The ODH page (last dated 11/17/2022) only requires the application, the $250 fee, the primary owner's fingerprint card and, for new providers, a $20,000 surety bond. I could not open the ODH application PDF, so the item list comes from the controlling rule, OAC 3701-60-03(B). For the ODH license, submit the application packet with (1) a list of nonmedical services and related policies and procedures, (2) the written criminal records check policy, (3) a statement of days and hours of operation, and (4) a description of the geographic area served. These are items (B)(3)(d), (g), (h) and (i). Items (B)(3)(d) to (k) are waived for providers holding ODA certification (3701-60-03(E)). Items (B)(3)(d) to (i) are waived for providers accredited by ACHC, CHAP, the Joint Commission or another approved national organization (3701-60-03(F)). For ODA PASSPORT certification, ODA does not publish a policy-manual checklist. It requires written or electronic policies on job descriptions and PCA qualification records (173-39-02.11(C)(5)), an incident-documentation policy (173-39-02(A)(7)), written theft or property-damage claim instructions (173-39-02(A)(5)(b)), and policies, bylaws or articles that bind employees to the 173-39-02(B)(8) conduct standards (173-39-02(C)(1)(c)). Organize the manual to follow these rule paragraph numbers so a reviewer can map each policy to its citation. The ODM rules (OAC 5160-46-04 and 5160-58-04) were not fetched in this pass, so no items from them are listed. The ODA certification rules also call for an organization table, ownership disclosures and attestations, but these are disclosure paperwork and not policy content, so they are excluded. Where an item above is a duty and not a literally required 'policy', the manual should still address it. Examples are the 3701-60-06 criminal records check steps, the 173-39-02(B)(3) reporting duties and the 173-39-02.11(C)(3)-(4) training and supervision rules.
